A map of the Horn of Africa in the late 19th century showing the Ethiopian Empire. Key locations to mark include the old capital Gondar in the northwest, the fortress of Magdala in the centre, the region of Shewa (Shoa) to the south, and the coastal area of Eritrea by the Red Sea. A dashed arrow shows the route of the British Napier expedition (1868) marching inland from the Red Sea coast to Magdala.

A simple horizontal timeline of 19th-century Ethiopia. Markers along a central line: 1855 (Kassa Hailu crowned Emperor Theodore II); 1868 (British expedition and death of Theodore at Magdala); 1889 (Menelik II crowned; Treaty of Wuchale signed with Italy); 1893 (Menelik denounces the Treaty of Wuchale); 1896 (Ethiopian victory at the Battle of Adwa). Clean flat textbook style, bold dates.
